content.p: This Act is the Counter-Terrorism Legislation Amendment Act (No. 1) 2018.

Each provision of this Act specified in column 1 of the table commences, or is taken to have commenced, in accordance with column 2 of the table. Any other statement in column 2 has effect according to its terms.

content.p: Note: This table relates only to the provisions of this Act as originally enacted. It will not be amended to deal with any later amendments of this Act.
Any information in column 3 of the table is not part of this Act. Information may be inserted in this column, or information in it may be edited, in any published version of this Act.

Legislation that is specified in a Schedule to this Act is amended or repealed as set out in the applicable items in the Schedule concerned, and any other item in a Schedule to this Act has effect according to its terms.

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: After Subdivision C of Division 104 of the Criminal Code

content.p: Insert:
Subdivision CA—Varying an interim control order
An application to vary an interim control order may be made to the issuing court by:
the person in relation to whom the order is made; or
a senior AFP member.
Note: For example, an application may be made to vary an interim control order to reflect a change in the mobile telephone number of the person in relation to whom the order is made.
The issuing court may vary the interim control order, but only if the court is satisfied that:
written consent to the variation has been given by:
if the application is made by the person in relation to whom the order is made—a senior AFP member; or
if the application is made by a senior AFP member—the person in relation to whom the order is made; and
the variation does not involve adding any obligations, prohibitions or restrictions to the order; and
the variation is appropriate in the circumstances.
A variation begins to be in force when the order for the variation is made, or at a later time ordered by the issuing court.
Omit “Before”, substitute “Subject to subsection (3A), before”.

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: After Subdivision C of Division 3A of Part IAA

content.p: Insert:
Subdivision CA—Reporting on exercise of powers under this Division

As soon as practicable after the exercise of a power or powers by an AFP police officer (or officers) under Subdivision B in relation to an incident, the Commissioner must give a report to the following:
the Minister;
the Independent National Security Legislation Monitor;
the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Intelligence and Security.
The report must state, in relation to the incident:
the number of instances when an AFP police officer (or officers) exercised a power under section 3UE, 3UEA or 3UF; and
the circumstances in which an AFP police officer (or officers) exercised powers under section 3UC or 3UD.
Note: The nature of these powers is as follows:
for section 3UC—requirement to provide names etc.;
for section 3UD—stopping and searching;
for section 3UE—seizure of terrorism related items and serious offence related items;
for section 3UEA—emergency entry to premises without a warrant;
for section 3UF—seizure notices.
(3) An AFP police officer is a member or a special member of the Australian Federal Police (within the meaning of the Australian Federal Police Act 1979).
Note: AFP police officers are police officers within the meaning of this Division (see section 3UA).

section.heading: Annual report on exercise of powers

content.p: The Minister must, as soon as practicable after each 30 June, cause to be prepared a report about the exercise of powers under this Division, during the year ended on that 30 June.
Without limiting subsection (1), a report relating to a year must include the following matters:
the number of instances when an AFP police officer (or officers) exercised a power under section 3UE, 3UEA or 3UF;
the number of incidents when an AFP police officer (or officers) exercised powers under section 3UC or 3UD;
the number of applications made under section 3UI for declarations that Commonwealth places are prescribed security zones;
the number of declarations made under section 3UJ that Commonwealth places are prescribed security zones.
The Minister must cause copies of the report to be laid before each House of the Parliament within 15 sitting days of that House after the report is completed.
(4) An AFP police officer is a member or a special member of the Australian Federal Police (within the meaning of the Australian Federal Police Act 1979).
Note: AFP police officers are police officers within the meaning of this Division (see section 3UA).
Omit “7 September 2018”, substitute “7 September 2021”.

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: At the end of Division 106 of the Criminal Code

content.p: Add:

(1) The amendment of subsection 104.5(1A) made by the Counter-Terrorism Legislation Amendment Act (No. 1) 2018 (the amending Act) applies in relation to an interim control order made on or after the day (the commencement day) this section commences, including such an order that was requested before the commencement day.
Note 1: Section 104.5 deals with the terms of an interim control order.
Note 2: This section was inserted by the amending Act.
Subdivision CA of Division 104 of this Act, as inserted by the amending Act, applies in relation to an interim control order made before, on or after the commencement day.
Note: Subdivision CA of Division 104 deals with the variation of an interim control order.
Subsection 104.14(3A) of this Act, as inserted by the amending Act, applies in relation to proceedings for the confirmation of an interim control order:
if the proceedings start on or after the commencement day; and
whether the original request for the interim control order was made before, on or after the commencement day.
Note: Subsection 104.14(3A) deals with the evidentiary status in confirmation proceedings of such an original request.
Section 104.28AA of this Act, as inserted by the amending Act, applies in relation to the proceedings in relation to a control order (including proceedings to vary or revoke a control order) if:
the proceedings start on or after the commencement day; or
the proceedings had started, but not ended, immediately before the commencement day.
Note: Section 104.28AA deals with costs in control order proceedings.

Subsections 119.3(5A) and (6) of this Act, as substituted by the amending Act, apply in relation to a declaration of the Foreign Affairs Minister made under subsection 119.3(1) before, on or after the commencement day.
Note: Subsections 119.3(5A) and (6) deal with the revocation of declarations made under subsection 119.3(1).
